description: Runs from the cluster (kubernetes/prod/services/renovate/). Every update is a pull request for the owner to merge; nothing merges itself.

customManagers.description: CloudNativePG clusters name their image as imageName, which the kubernetes manager doesn't read.
Kubernetes's version for the Talos cluster: kubernetes_version in tofu/proxmox/talos-config.tf.
Talos's version: the installer image's tag in talos/patches/common.yaml (the schematic ID before it stays).
A version Renovate can't otherwise read (a Dockerfile ARG, or a chart value naming its image as registry), marked by a '# renovate: datasource=<d> depName=<name>' comment on the line above.

packageRules.description: Stable releases only. ignoreUnstable (set above, config:recommended's default) skips what a versioning scheme can tell is a pre-release; this also refuses any tag naming one, and the images pin full versions, since a tag pinned to a minor (valkey's 9.2-alpine was 9.2.0-rc1) carries no suffix to tell by (QUEUE-updates.md).
A captured release is updated through its generated files; regenerate so release.yaml, values.yaml and the generated files agree (scripts/renovate_post_upgrade.py).
A database's major version is a migration (QUEUE-updates.md), not a version bump: listed on the Dependency Dashboard, opened only when ticked there. Likewise Whisparr's v3, a different app.
vectorchord's tags are <PostgreSQL major>-<extension version>: only the extension moves.
linuxserver tags are the app's version plus the image's own build (-ls<n>), which moves on a rebuild of the same app version.

Lidarr runs its nightly channel, for qBittorrent's API key (stable has gone without a release since 3.1.0): its pinned tag is nightly-<version>-ls<n>, followed only to later nightlies. Back to stable tags once a stable release passes the nightly pinned (QUEUE.md).
qBittorrent's tags add the libtorrent version: <qBittorrent>_v<libtorrent>-ls<n>, kept to the same libtorrent.
A chart and the images its values pin move together: merging one without the other would run a new chart with an old image.
One pull request for the app-template chart across every release that uses it.
OpenTofu, not Terraform: providers from OpenTofu's registry, and required_version (an exact OpenTofu version, matching Semaphore's) left to a hand update.

Kubernetes and Talos: a pull request for every release, ready for when the upgrade is wanted. Merging changes only tofu/proxmox/talos-config.tf or talos/patches/common.yaml, which Flux doesn't apply; the upgrade is the playbook, then the OpenTofu job (the playbooks' headers say why). Check the add-ons' support for a new Kubernetes minor first (QUEUE-updates.md).
prBodyNotes: Merging this changes nothing by itself. Run the upgrade playbook (`ansible/talos-k8s-upgrade.yml` for Kubernetes, `ansible/talos-upgrade.yml` for Talos) in check mode, then for real, and only then the OpenTofu job.

packageRules.description: The tools in docker/'s images are pinned without the v their GitHub tags carry.
Kea and Stork install from package sources named for their minor series (docker/kea/Dockerfile: kea-3-2), so a new minor is a migration, listed on the Dependency Dashboard, not a version bump.
homelab/* images are built on the Docker host from their Dockerfile (pull_policy: build), not pulled: there's nothing to look up.
NetBox's image and its plugins (docker/netbox/) move together: the image is built from both, and a plugin release often follows a NetBox one.
A NetBox minor or major release waits until every plugin supports it (docker/netbox/README.md): listed on the Dependency Dashboard, opened only when ticked there.
